I fetched the page. The quoted words are on it exactly, and I read the candidate as a **pass**.

**1. Is the quote on the page?** Yes, word for word. The page is Sundar Pichai's own Google blog post of his I/O 2022 keynote. The page names him as author and gives the date 2022-05-11. The sentence sits under the heading "Auto-translated captions on YouTube". It comes right after: "Next up, we're bringing auto-translated captions on YouTube to mobile… in 16 languages." The next section opens: "Just as we're using AI to improve features in YouTube…" Because these are his own words, the source counts as primary, not coverage.

**2. The four parts of the rule:**
- **Part 1, role: met.** On 2022-05-11 he was chief executive of Google (since 2015) and of Alphabet (since 2019).
- **Part 2, forward-looking and about AI: met, though I considered calling it borderline.** The search run flagged it as borderline because it is a small feature launch. But the rule says a product shipping counts when the product is an AI system and the words say something about its deployment. Auto-translated captions are machine translation, and the page itself presents them as AI ("we're using AI to improve features in YouTube"). The ledger already holds similar short-range launch claims from Pichai, such as the 2023 Magic Editor and 2024 AI Overviews files. So I don't think it is a truly borderline case.
- **Part 3, a date: met.** "Next month", said 11 May 2022, means June 2022, so the due date would be 2022-06-30.
- **Part 4, primary source: met.** It is his own published keynote text.

**Already recorded?** No. The only recorded claim from the same day is the YouTube auto-chapters "80 million" goal, which is a different claim from the same keynote.
